title: MAUnet: Multiscale Attention U-Net for Effective IR Drop Prediction
problem: Full-chip static IR drop prediction in ultra deep-submicron VLSI designs is computationally challenging. Conventional modified nodal analysis methods are inefficient for analyzing power grids with shrinking power supply voltages.
motivation: Accurate and efficient IR drop prediction is essential for ensuring reliable IC designs as technology nodes advance and power budgets tighten.
method: MAUnet uses a U-Net neural network (an architecture that processes circuit data like an image) with multi-scale blocks that zoom in and out to detect both fine details and overall patterns. Attention mechanisms identify voltage hotspots—the areas where drops are worst. Because the power grid is formatted as an image, the method scales to chips of any size. It uses low-rank approximation transfer learning, which lets it generalize to new, unseen circuits.
key_novelty: It represents power grid data as images, enabling image-processing neural networks to predict voltage drops accurately across chips of any size.
contributions: MAUnet architecture integrating multi-scale convolutions, attention mechanisms, and U-Net for full-chip IR drop prediction
Novel data fusion method combining power grid and image-based representations
Low-rank approximation transfer learning for generalization to unseen circuits
Achieves <6% average error with 29-68% improvement over IREDGe and orders of magnitude speedup versus commercial tools

metrics.accuracy: Average error <6% relative to average IR drop
metrics.speedup: Orders of magnitude compared to commercial tools
